requirements.requirement: On node1, /tmp ignores program execution, setuid bits, and device nodes, and the hardening survives reboot.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, /tmp was a tmpfs mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev. Execution and device-access probes failed as expected, the persistent fstab entry validated, and the post-reboot directory retained mode 1777.

requirements.requirement: On node1, /dev/shm ignores program execution, setuid bits, and device nodes, and the hardening survives reboot.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, /dev/shm was mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev. Execution and device-access probes failed as expected, the persistent fstab entry validated, and the post-reboot directory retained mode 1777.

overall_summary: Both mount-hardening outcomes are satisfied and directly demonstrated across a real reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, changed boot ID from 54089086-53d1-408b-a22f-57b1dea70e03 to c5aee522-9f9a-4712-915b-6579729d46c0, returned to running state, and recovered the hardened mounts. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: There was no behavioral setuid-execution probe; nosuid is established through direct live mount-option observations before and after reboot.
The presumed retained /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening backup was not included in a final filesystem inventory, so its final presence is inferred from creation with no captured removal.

There was no application-specific data or cluster state to verify on this single-node mount-hardening task; recovery evidence instead covers system state, mount state, listening services, and package health.

operational_hygiene.summary: The configuration, temporary test files, device nodes, and reboot were directly connected to implementation, bounded verification, or persistence testing; test artifacts and the staging fstab file were removed. One minor unnecessary retained mutation is indicated: cmd-65142f39789e4aa2 created /etc/fstab.pre-mount-hardening, and no later command removed it. This rollback copy was prudent while changing fstab but became residual after successful validation. No failed services, new exposure, or package damage was observed after execution.
